text:
SupportEngineer_Ana: Pasting customer report from AcmePay — they started getting large numbers of 429s around 2025-11-03T09:12Z after a scheduled retry job. They claim their SDK backoff is exponential but still seeing sustained failures. Quote from their logs: 

Customer (pasted): '429 rate_limit_exceeded rpm=110 tpm=660 for key sk-prod-*** — spikes happen when our batch-retry process flattens into many small concurrent requests'

SupportEngineer_Ana: I captured sample response headers they forwarded: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rate-limit-rpm: 100
x-rate-limit-tpm: 600
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-request-id: req_0a1b2c3d
Retry-After: 30
```

SRE_Ravi: mhm. Looks like they hit per-key RPM cap (100) and hit tpm bucket. Do we have any recent config changes to the rate limiter or proxy tokens?

SDK_Lead_Mike: nothing infra-side. but SDK default backoff for batch jobs is 1s linear with max 16s in older builds — that can still create synchronized retry storms if many items retry together. Are they using older SDK?

SupportEngineer_Ana: They are on sdk-js v2.1.0 (we shipped v2.2.5 with jittered exponential backoff earlier this year). Customer says they run a fan-out that turns a single cron into ~250 parallel requests.

Dev_PM_Lisa: Key questions: Is this strictly per-key throttle, or are there upstream proxy/pool limits (per-IP, per-organization)? Also want to confirm whether the bursts are short-lived (seconds) or sustained (minutes).

SRE_Ravi: From infra metrics (quick look): for that customer key at 09:12Z we saw a sharp plateau: rpm ~115 for ~7 minutes, tpm crossed 650 at 09:17. Downstream, our token-bucket replenishes per 60s window, so sustained parallelism will bleed quota. I also see a secondary spike of retries 09:19 likely from client retry loop.

InfraBot: Automated snapshot created: /snapshots/1950001111-acmepay-429-20251103.json (includes per-route rpm/tpm charts, top 100 request ids).

SupportEngineer_Ana: Customer asks for immediate mitigation — what can we offer while they upgrade SDK or change retry schedule?

SRE_Ravi: Short-term options: 
- Issue a temporary per-key quota bump (support action) — we can increase RPM/TMP for a single key for up to 24h, but must gate it behind manual review.
- Apply per-route burst allowance if route is low-risk.
- Suggest client-side quick mitigations: add jitter, randomize retry window, cap concurrency to 20 concurrent connections.

SDK_Lead_Mike: I can provide a small patch snippet they can paste into their retry wrapper to break synchronization: 
```
// quick jittered backoff example (node)
const base = 1000; // 1s
function jitteredBackoff(attempt){
  const exp = Math.min(16000, base * Math.pow(2, attempt));
  const jitter = Math.floor(Math.random() * 500);
  return exp + jitter;
}
```

SupportEngineer_Ana: I told them to try client cap + jitter AND to send a short curl that reproduces the 429 quickly so we can attach request ids. Example I asked for: 
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-REDACTED" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"input":"x"}'
```

Dev_PM_Lisa: For the longer term: consider suggesting they use our rate-limiter-aware SDK integration (v2.2.5+) which does adaptive throttling based on x-rate-limit-* headers and exposes a "concurrencyLimit" override. Also document recommended patterns for batch workers (queue + token bucket at client side).

SRE_Ravi: I can do the temporary per-key bump if support signs off. Quick checklist before bump: confirm customer identity, confirm non-abusive traffic (already looked at top endpoints), get written acknowledgement they will throttle retries, and schedule a revert in 24h.

SupportEngineer_Ana: I have identity + screenshot of their deployment that shows the cron schedule. They agreed to implement cap within 2 hours. Proceed with bump?

Dev_PM_Lisa: Approve, but add a safety rule: set a soft limit alert at 90% of new quota and enable auto-fallback to a cheaper model tier if we see costs escalate.

SDK_Lead_Mike: Also opened a small PR to the SDK repo with a rate-limit header parser and example usage — will DM link shortly.

SRE_Ravi: Done — temporary bump applied: rpm=250 tpm=1500 for key sk-prod-REDACTED until 2025-11-04T09:30Z. I recorded action id: act_1950001111_bump. Monitor dashboards for two cycles pls.

SupportEngineer_Ana: Noted. Customer is running their job now with concurrency capped at 30 and jitter applied — initial results show success rate improved from ~60% to ~95% within 2 minutes. They still see occasional 429s but much less noisy.

InfraBot: Alert rule added: watch/key/sk-prod-REDACTED at 85% -> ping @SRE_Ravi @SupportEngineer_Ana.

Dev_PM_Lisa: Follow-up actions: 
- Support: send step-by-step mitigation email + SDK patch (Ana)
- SRE: schedule quota revert and postmortem note if needed (Ravi)
- SDK: publish minor release with jittered backoff and header-aware throttling (Mike)

SupportEngineer_Ana: Will send the email and ask customer to confirm once they deploy the SDK patch. Marking this thread for handoff to postmortem if we see bounceback. :thumbsup:

SRE_Ravi: Flagging for postmortem if we see repeat in 72h. Closing interim triage.

SDK_Lead_Mike: PR link: https://git.internal.redwood/sdk-js/pulls/842 (internal).

SupportEngineer_Ana: Thanks all.
